hypothesis: A bounded extension of each S6 fit by four adjacent saved events on either side reduces period variance from 20-ms event quantization, while residual and count checks expose unsupported timing instead of creating or removing beats.

algorithm.name: s6-four-neighbor-ols-v1
algorithm.window_partition: unchanged six source-local S6 windows per recording; each accepted window is one constant-period diagnostic segment; no adaptive split or merge
algorithm.fit: exact rational ordinary least squares of source frames against original consecutive event indices over all in-window events plus up to four adjacent events on either side, clipped only at source boundaries
algorithm.tempo: round 48000*60000/fitted_period to nearest millibpm, ties upward; require 40000..300000 inclusive; publish period floor((48000*60000<<32)/tempo)
algorithm.anchor: evaluate the exact fitted line at the first original in-window event ordinal and round to integer source frame, ties upward; keep original global event ordinal; require anchor within the unchanged window
algorithm.residual: require every support event within two original feature hops (1920 frames) of its corresponding published Q32 line, including neighbor support; this is a fixed model-consistency guard, not a reference tolerance
algorithm.event_identity: the Q32 line enumerated from the anchor to the unchanged window end must contain exactly the original in-window event count; retain the one-to-one original global ordinals and reject count changes, never repair or truncate
algorithm.boundaries: require all neighboring accepted window points to remain strictly ordered with consecutive global ordinals; analysis abstention creates unknown support, not a known PCM gap; never bridge it or assert complete-source coverage
algorithm.gaps_and_ambiguity: explicit declared PCM gaps reject affected context before fitting; missing or extra musical events are not declared PCM gaps; residual/support/count/tempo failures abstain without fallback, half/double-tempo search, phase rescue or silent event deletion
algorithm.meter: retain the raw two-complete-equal-bars support rule inside the original window; map that original downbeat ordinal onto this window's published Q32 line and require its whole frame within the same window; never borrow another grid or reference meter
algorithm.confidence: uncalibrated, placeholder zero; never a safety PASS or stable/final result

evaluation.control: reproduce all saved OLS tuples and old score_window verdicts and old coarse scores before comparison; old scorer and event-representation diagnostics unchanged
evaluation.candidate: score the same six unchanged window ranges with the frozen constant-grid score_window, plus the unchanged common point/period and one-to-one sequence diagnostics
evaluation.paired: record period/phase/joint fixes and breaks against both OLS and coarse; report both original coarse-to-OLS regressions separately
evaluation.meter: record same-grid meter numerator/denominator and downbeat correctness, support/abstention changes, and individual old-correct-to-wrong or missing transitions
evaluation.run_order: single fixed 100-source cohort in its existing manifest order, all 600 windows retained; evaluate the aggregate veto once after this complete cohort; no subsequent corpus or parameter search after veto failure
evaluation.identity_or_baseline_failure: stop immediately; no successful algorithm result
evaluation.failure_action: reject and preserve this exact candidate; no same-cohort threshold, context, fallback or model rescue
